messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary slice r15 showing post-deploy regression. p99 latency ~4x, throughput down ~30%, error spike 5xx. Auto-paged to #incidents. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abc123

alice: I'm connected. p50 is fine but p95/p99 spiking. Logs show repeated 'kernel fallback' and 'kv eviction' events. Started right after canary stepped to 10% traffic (~T+30s).

gabe: grabbing logs now, snippets:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:32Z host=r15-runtime svc=rpc msg=\"kernel fallback\" reason=\"prefetch-pool-saturated\" kv_evictions=512
2026-03-15T09:12:45Z host=r15-runtime svc=rpc latency_p99=2300ms
```

priya: Which customers are hitting that canary? Any big tenants on r15? Need to surface CSMs.

alice: Two tenants on canary: acme-inc and atlas-sf for an A/B test. Acme reporting a support surge — errors up ~10% 5xx. Ticket INC-9876 created.

marco: Suspect the new prefetch/pooling tweak in the release. Prefetch v2 bumped worker/concurrency defaults and appears to saturate the KV prefetch workers under bursty client patterns, causing memory pressure and kernel fallback. Also seeing batching collapse when pool saturates.

elena: We can flip the feature kill-switch for prefetch_v2 for the canary slice quickly. That should revert to legacy prefetch behavior without a full rollback. Recommend try kill-flag first.

luis: Agreed. Kill-flag should short-circuit the new pool and restore the stable path; should reduce kv_evictions and let batching recover.

alice: Issuing kill-flag now:
```
$ rctl feature-toggle set prefetch_v2_enabled=false --env=prod --selector=slice=r15
# auth: admin-token
```

alice: kill-flag applied at 1767654350

incident-bot: action recorded: feature-toggle(prefetch_v2_enabled=false) by alice at 1767654350

gabe: Watching metrics: within ~40s p99 falling from ~2300ms -> ~480ms, throughput climbing back. Kernel fallback logs dropping.

priya: Acme support update: they see errors drop to ~2% now. I'll post a quick status update to their ticket and ping CSMs. :white_check_mark:

marco: While the kill-flag bought time, we should roll the canary back to the previous stable binary that doesn't contain prefetch_v2. Flag is a short-term safety net.

elena: Starting canary rollback to v14 (stable) now:
```
$ deployctl promote --from stable --to canary --version=v14 --force
```

elena: rollback initiated at 1767654410

alice: Post-rollback metrics: throughput within 95% of baseline, p99 ~420ms, kernel-fallback events gone. Prefetch_v2 remains disabled until we complete triage.

luis: Preliminary root cause: prefetch_v2 default concurrency too high for small canary slices; combined with client burstiness this caused KV thrash and memory pressure -> runtime selected fallback kernel and batching thinned out. Follow-ups: add hard caps on prefetch concurrency, surface prefetch pool occupancy metric to Console, and implement a graceful degrade path that rejects new prefetch requests rather than thrashing.

priya: Customer impact summary for incident doc:
- window: 1767654321 -> 1767654460 (~2.3 minutes)
- impacted tenants: acme-inc (10% 5xx spike), atlas-sf (1-2% spike)
- mitigation: feature kill-flag flipped (alice) -> rapid improvement
- rollback: canary promoted back to v14 (elena)
- status: resolved on canary, stable unaffected, monitoring for residuals

alice: Handoff to next on-call. @marco will own follow-ups for 72h, @luis to drive code fixes, @elena to validate canary with reduced concurrency and coordinate safe re-roll.

marco: Taking handoff. I'll open the incident doc with reproducer (load script + exact flags), add timelines, and action items: [1] concurrency cap, [2] console visibility for kill-flags and pool metrics, [3] runbook update for prefetch regressions.

incident-bot: incident page created -> https://incidents.redwood/INC-20260315-42

priya: I'll draft customer comms and a short blameless note for acme support. Adding to incident doc now.

alice: Thanks all — leaving channel at 1767654765. Handoff complete. Please append any additional logs or timelines to the incident page.
